scope: Offline counterfactual scheduling, not implemented RTL or timing closure
assumptions: A result-owner handoff at qualified inverse publication parks its actual reader obligation; it does not assert a fake reader ACK.
The proposed eight-cycle core dispatch preserves existing registered completion, two reset states and two discovery edges; its context handoff at publication is not implemented or measured.
Only one next forward may run while the previous inverse output is retained; the next inverse requires actual old-output final read ACK and cleared parked context.
Source producers obey the original bounded eager testbench offer schedule, including its interblock gap and profile1 pauses; this is not a native source capacity proof.
Raw FFT service cycle counts are held constant only for conditional frequency arithmetic. No other clock or vendor implementation has been evaluated.
The original noncoincident ideal clock phases and finite ready patterns are modeled in integer femtoseconds; arbitrary stalls and metastability are outside this throughput estimate.
Both actual FIFOs remain real mailbox banks. Core-local resets may not clear retained payload, lease, ACK state, or common epoch faults.
Current phase_lost, raw_orphan and shared guard_busy references must be split by actual core-job versus retained-consumer ownership before this schedule is legal.
The two-bit lease is not sufficient for arbitrarily stale references; empty producer/certificate/reader references and fresh common-reset CDC rearm remain mandatory.
